candidates.review_note: Bitset transitive closure determines the maximum relation after removing reflexive pairs. Vertices with identical reflexive reachability rows are exactly the strongly connected components. Each nontrivial component can be represented by a directed cycle of its size. Between components, the condensation DAG has a unique transitive reduction; process each outgoing neighbor in decreasing reachable-set size, retaining an edge only when its target is not already covered by a previously retained successor. This counts the required cover edges without requiring the new edges to occur in the original graph.

A fixed-point transformation partitions positions and values into the same consecutive blocks. Each block is one permutation cycle and begins with its largest value; a block of size s>=2 has(s-2)! possibilities. Count compositions with these block weights, then unrank by the first block maximum. Within a block, assign remaining permutation entries lexicographically while disallowing a premature cycle: partial edges form disjoint directed paths, and joining the remaining path components into one cycle has a factorial number of completions. DSU detects premature closure; the final edge is allowed to close the full cycle. Exact integers avoid saturation errors for ranks up to10^18.
